title: From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Pay Like Pauline Hanson's Salary
description: Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual salary using the standard 38-hour week. Compare with the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and even Pauline Hanson's salary.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming a 38-hour week for full-time work.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour yields $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,261.44 per year.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the Fair Work system are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for entitlements like paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 + 25% = $33.05 per hour. When using our calculator, you can check the casual loading box to add 25% to your base rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated and is it included in my annual salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at a rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not part of your gross salary; your employer must pay it separately into your super fund. For example, if your annual salary is $70,000, your employer contributes an additional $8,400 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Our calculator estimates super on ordinary earnings only.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: Understanding Your Pay Like Pauline Hanson's Salary

Whether you're a casual worker earning the National Minimum Wage or a high-profile politician like Pauline Hanson, the method for converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is the same. Understanding this conversion helps you compare job offers, budget, and plan for tax and super. This guide explains the formula, the role of the 38-hour week, and how to use our [the timesheet](/) calculator.

## The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This gives your gross annual pay before any deductions. For a full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage. For example:

- National Minimum Wage: $26.44/hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $52,261.44 per year.
- A casual worker on $30/hour (before loading) working 38 hours: $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year.

If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Our calculator lets you enter your actual hours per week.

### Why 38 Hours?

The 38-hour week is the standard full-time ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act. It is used for the National Minimum Wage and many awards. However, some awards or agreements may define full-time as 40 hours. Always check your award or contract. For part-time or casual work, use your actual average weekly hours.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the minimum for award/agreement-free employees. Most workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Clerks Award or Hospitality Award have specific pay rates for each classification. Use our [pay guides](/blog) to find the correct rate for your job.

Even a high-profile salary like Pauline Hanson's is calculated using the same hourly-to-annual conversion. While her exact hourly rate is not publicly listed, Senators and MPs receive a base salary determined by the Remuneration Tribunal, which is well above the national average. The formula still applies: annual salary ÷ (hours per week × 52) gives an equivalent hourly rate.

## Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (sick leave, annual leave). For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 + 25% = $33.05 per hour. When using our [the timesheet](/) calculator, check the "Casual loading" box to automatically add 25% to your base rate. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator adds it for you.

## Superannuation (Paid on Top)

Superannuation is an additional payment from your employer, not part of your gross salary. From 1 July 2026, the Super Guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer contributes $9,600 in super. Our calculator estimates super on ordinary earnings only, assuming no salary sacrifice or other arrangements.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 + 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 + 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 + 45% of excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed estimate.

## Using the Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you enter your base hourly rate and weekly hours. It shows your annual gross, fortnightly pay (weekly × 2), estimated tax, Medicare, and super. The fortnightly figure is useful for budgeting if you're paid bi-weekly. Remember, the estimate assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. For precise calculations, refer to your award or agreement.

## Conclusion

Converting hourly to annual is simple: multiply by hours per week and 52. Whether you're comparing your rate to the National Minimum Wage or a politician's salary like Pauline Hanson's, the math is the same. Use our calculator to see your annual, fortnightly, and take-home pay, and always check your award or agreement for the correct minimum rates.
